attributes.body:
In the same way as the case marking particleと means 'and', sometimes it is translated as 'if'. In these cases, it is considered to be far stronger than ば, なら, or たら (which express hypothetical outcomes). This is because one of the primary uses of と is highlighting a result. In these cases, と is actually a conjunction particle, and shows one of three things.

仮定（かてい）の順接（じゅんせつ） - A result that is assumed to be true, and obvious.

確定（かくてい）の順接（じゅんせつ） - A result that is known to be true.

仮定（かてい）の逆接（ぎゃくせつ） - The opposite of a result that is assumed to be true.

Due to this, the (B) part of a phrase using と as 'if', will always occur when (A) happens, as it is considered to be the result of (A).

と may not be used in situations where the (B) result 'might' happen. It must be definite (or close to definite).

In this particular nuance of と, despite being translated as 'if', the actual meaning is much closer to 'and', as と is expressing that (A) and (B) will always go together.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: "IF" / "WHEN" （と vs たら vs とき) Differences ┃PART1 & 2

attributes.body: と marks a natural condition, while そうすると is used to explain what would happen in that case. It means 'if that happens' or 'then...' and often introduces a result. For example, 早く寝なさい。そうすると、明日は元気になるよ ('Go to bed early. Then you'll feel good tomorrow.')

first_relatable.title: そうすると
first_relatable.meaning: Having done that..., If that is done..., (And/just) then, Thereupon, If so

attributes.body: と is used to express natural or habitual results, as in 春が来ると花が咲く ('When spring comes, flowers bloom.'). もし adds emphasis to conditionals and can appear before と or other conditionals like たら and ば. For example, もし雨が降ったら 'if it rains' has a more hypothetical tone than if もし were not present.

ば and と are both conditional expressions, but differ in nuance. ば emphasizes the condition that leads to a result, often with an 'if and only if' tone. と is used for habitual or automatic outcomes, suggesting that what follows happens naturally or inevitably when the condition is met.

たら and と are both conditional forms, but they differ in nuance and usage. たら expresses both 'if' and 'when', and can describe hypotheticals or one-time events, such as 雨が降ったら行きません ('If it rains, I won't go.'). と is used for regular or expected outcomes, as in 春になると桜が咲く ('When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.').

first_relatable.title: たら
first_relatable.meaning: When, From when, Just when, If

attributes.body: と marks a natural result, while すると is a transition word meaning 'thereupon' or 'and then'. It's often used at the beginning of a new sentence to show what happened next. For example, ドアを開けた。すると、猫がいた ('I opened the door. And there was a cat.'

first_relatable.title: すると
first_relatable.meaning: Having done..., If...is done..., (And/just) then, Thereupon, If so

attributes.body: Both と and なら are conditional expressions, but differ in nuance. と is used for habitual or automatic results, e.g. 春になると花が咲く ('When it becomes spring, flowers bloom.'). なら is used for one-time or assumed situations and implies the speaker believes the condition is likely, e.g. 雨なら出かけない ('If it's going to rain, I won't go out.').

second_relatable.title: なら
second_relatable.meaning: Were it, If, If it's the case, As for (Conditional)

attributes.body: と and ばあいは can both express conditions, but differ significantly in usage. と describes something that happens habitually or as a natural result, e.g. お酒を飲むとすぐ酔っ払ってしまう ('When I drink alcohol, I get drunk quickly.'). ばあいは is used more for situational instructions, like お酒を飲む場合は運転しないほうがいい ('In the event that you drink alcohol, you shouldn't drive.').

second_relatable.title: ばあいは
second_relatable.meaning: In the event of, In the case of
